# Independent audit: weighted facet residual credit and two-input erosion

**PASS**, with the standard Borell--Brascamp--Lieb theorem as the explicitly
stated external mathematical dependency. I read all six sections of
`candidate 4283399302c56a21`.
No correction is required. This audit checks the application and its exact
geometric/status hypotheses; it does not reprove BBL or independently
validate the bibliographic location of the linked statement.

## Weight and dimension

The tangent continuation remains positive, decreasing and convex on the
entire real line. Its negative power `g=f^(-1/d)` has the displayed
positive second derivative below the join and matching derivative one
at the join, hence is globally convex. Therefore the pairwise inequality
has the correct direction for BBL with negative exponent: from

    w_K(mid)^(-1/d) <= [w_A^(-1/d)+w_B^(-1/d)]/2

one obtains `w_K(mid)>=M_{-1/d}(w_A,w_B)`. The intrinsic dimension is
`k=d-1`; thus `p=-1/d>-1/k` and `p/(1+kp)=-1`. These are exactly the
hypotheses and exponent giving the harmonic mass lower bound. No
limiting full-dimensional exponent is substituted. Restricted positive
supports, open residual sets and zero-mass inputs are handled correctly.

## Same ambient halfspace and support statuses

At an active support normal, both the face midpoint inclusion and the
captured/missed midpoint implications concern the original ambient cap,
including its original integer coefficient. Positive weighted residuals
are measured in that same actual facet geometry. Consequently the two
inequalities (2), and their joint-event versions, use a single set of
physical face measures rather than freely chosen cap marginals.

The supporting-face trace argument is valid. Translating the abstract
input faces inward by positive amounts and the middle face by their
average preserves the exact midpoint inclusion. The affine cap margins
also average exactly. With a fixed continuous density, dominated
convergence gives the inward capture bits, including a whole coincident
face. For proper facet cuts the exceptional tangent boundary is
intrinsically null. Pure integer cap margins remain constant under these
translations, so a fiber on the closed integer boundary remains captured;
no open-halfspace convention is silently introduced. The translated
faces need not be actual parallel sections, and the source does not
claim that they are.

## Scalar residual optimization

For residual masses `s,t` of fixed sum `S>b_0`, the endpoint interval is
`S-b_0<=s<=a_0`. Its product minimum is at `s=S-b_0,t=b_0`, because

    b_0(S-b_0)-a_0(S-a_0)
      =(b_0-a_0)(S-a_0-b_0)<=0.

Thus `R>=2b_0(S-b_0)/S` gives the stated cap-credit lower bound.
The positive branch ends exactly at `R=Harm(a_0,b_0)`, where its value
is zero. All divisions have positive denominators in their stated
domains. The displayed equality choices certify sharpness of this
scalar constraint only, as appropriately distinguished from actual
geometric equality on a specified triple.

## Actual simultaneous erosion and cost normalization

The fields in (4) are continuous, nonnegative and physically convex even
when their normal-dependent centers lie outside the input bodies. Their
boundedness on compact neighborhoods supplies a positive inner homothet
for small parameters. Convexity of `f` and `c_A+c_B=2y` give

    (Psi_A(n,x)+Psi_B(n,x'))/2
      >=H(n) f(1+a.((x+x')/2-y)).

Together with the original support inequality `h_M<=h_K`, this proves
the exact target erosion inclusion for all normals, without any
source-in-midpoint or common-fan premise. The audited continuum-normal
first-variation theorem supplies the actual boundary losses, with the
same inward selectors checked above.

At an active facet the three density masses multiply the SAME factor
`H(n)`, yielding precisely (6) and total cost
`H(n)(a_0+b_0+m_0)`. These are not the masses of the separate one-input
construction, whose arguments contain a midpoint with a minimizing
partner and whose factor is `2H`. The source explicitly preserves this
distinction and makes no global payment or OC claim.
